newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House Banking Democrats support bill mix.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House Banking Democrats support bill mix.

text.p: Democrats on the House Banking Committee would support banking legislation that combined the Senate version of regulatory relief and the House proposal to bolster the undercapitalized Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF), a spokeswoman for the Democrats said.
"House Banking Committee Democrats think this is the best possible outcome," she told reporters.
Rep. James Leach, R-Iowa, chairman of the committee, said the current path being considered is to attach banking legislation to a continuing resolution, a short-term spending bill.
Leach said there was no "prejudging" the exact shape of the final banking legislation and all issues were on the table, including provisions related to insurance.
On regulatory relief, Leach said the differences between the House and Senate versions were "reconcilable, but I suspect you'll get a little from each side."

The SAIF proposal would require thrifts to pay a one-time charge to boost the fund to its mandated level. Currently thrifts would need to pay a total of $4.7 billion to recapitalize the SAIF, a committee spokesman said.
Leach said he was optimistic that banking legislation would move this session.
